PullRequest.Title: Agent host worktree locations: the provider names its own locations
PullRequest.Body:

## What

The agent host's worktree location provider names its own locations ("Worktrees") instead of borrowing the workbench's `getWorktreesLabel()`. The status bar folder location switcher already sections locations by their provider's label, so the label now comes from the provider that contributes them. No behavior change.

## Changes

- `agentHostWorktreeLocations.ts`: `AgentHostWorktreeLocationProvider.label` is localized in the provider (`agentHost.worktreeLocations.label`), no longer imported from `workbench/services/workspaces/common/folderLocationSections.ts`.

## Notes for reviewers

- The chat input folder picker and the sessions workspace picker are intentionally untouched; they keep their own sections and strings.
- The English text stays "Worktrees"; only the localization key changes.

## Validation

- `./scripts/test.sh --run agentHostWorktreeLocations, agentHostWorktreeFolderChoices, folderLocationSections, contrib/workspaces tests`: 83 passing
- `pnpm run typecheck-client`: passed
- `pnpm run oxlint <changed file>`: passed

Scenarios.Scenario: Instantiate the window's agent-host worktree provider and initialize its label.
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The delayed singleton initializes one readonly label during construction. Previously getWorktreesLabel() immediately called localize(); now construction calls localize() directly. Both perform synchronous in-memory string lookup/formatting.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: One constant-size label per provider instance, independent of session, folder, and worktree counts.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: One provider singleton per window; no asynchronous scheduling added.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: The readonly label is computed once and reused. Built localization reads the existing global NLS table; neither implementation initiates language-pack I/O.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: inspected both the deleted helper's body and localize/lookupMessage implementations; the replacement has the same localization cost and no boundary calls.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: No measurements; no added scaling or blocking mechanism identified.
Scenarios.Verdict: No regression. Only the localization key and ownership change; the import removal adds no eager module dependency or expensive initialization.

Scenarios.Scenario: Open the status-bar folder location switcher and display provider-labelled worktree groups.
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The picker displays seeded entries immediately, then asynchronously loads groups. WorkspaceFolderLocationService calls providers concurrently and copies the already-initialized label into results. This provider returns currently known sessions without awaiting its background session listing or realpath lookup.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Send the root-channel listSessions protocol request to the agent host and map its returned session summaries.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One inventory-wide request per cold/invalidation refresh, coalesced within this store; no calls on a warm valid cache. Existing mutation-generation races can trigger a further refresh.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Identical calls, coalescing, payload mapping, and scheduling; getWorktreesLabel already produced the same kind of group string.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Runs in the background for provideLocations; does not delay initial picker display.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: IFileService.realpath resolves the folder's canonical path.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One cached/coalesced operation per distinct successfully resolved workspace folder; failed requests can retry on later asks.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Identical per-folder cache keys, operation count, and background placement.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Started without awaiting by getFolderForms; known locations are returned first and changes notified later.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: One label per nonempty provider group, not per session. A cold provider session inventory uses one listSessions request for the entire inventory, not one per folder or worktree. Realpath scales with distinct requested workspace folders; displayed entries are URI-deduplicated.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Promise.all across registered providers. Within this provider, session refreshes share one in-flight promise; successful workspace-folder realpath requests share a cached promise per normalized folder. Session listing and realpath can proceed concurrently.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Warm valid session inventory avoids listSessions and notifications maintain it. Concurrent cold refreshes coalesce. Failed listings remain invalid and retry on subsequent asks. Successful workspace realpaths persist until folder retirement; failures evict for retry. Nonworkspace provideLocations calls do not initiate realpath reads.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: traced label consumers, picker loading, provider implementation, refresh coalescing, and the outbound session-list protocol request; no label-dependent discovery or additional calls exist.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Inventory size and host/filesystem latency are unmeasured, but none of their cardinality or scheduling changes in this diff.
Scenarios.Verdict: No regression. The new string feeds the existing group presentation without changing renderer count, discovery work, boundary fan-out, or retained state.

Scenarios.Scenario: Resolve an alternate folder location, including restoring a worktree before its sessions have loaded.
Scenarios.CriticalPath: WorkspaceFolderLocationService tries providers sequentially. This provider awaits folder forms, checks known sessions, and on a miss awaits the coalesced session refresh before checking again. Only after successful resolution does the service attach provider.label as group metadata.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Resolve the primary folder's realpath before matching a worktree.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One on a cold workspace-folder cache, zero when warm; one per resolution for an uncached nonworkspace primary, as before.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same awaited filesystem call and cache/coalescing policy.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Awaited before location matching, unchanged by the label replacement.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Await an inventory-wide listSessions request when cached sessions cannot yet resolve the target and the inventory is invalid.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One shared request per invalid inventory refresh, rather than one per session; zero when the store is valid. Existing invalidation races or later failed attempts may retry.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Identical request count, sequencing, and cancellation; the old helper-created label was attached at the same point.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Awaited for an unresolved target; group-label metadata is attached only after resolution succeeds.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: One canonical-path operation per uncached distinct folder and one shared inventory request on an invalid session cache, not one request per candidate worktree. Session matching scans cached summaries.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Providers are tried sequentially; concurrent requests to this provider share the inventory refresh and workspace-folder realpath promise. Lifetime and caller cancellation bound waiting.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Warm successful workspace-folder realpaths are reused. Warm session cache refreshes return without IPC, including when a requested worktree is absent. Failed listing/path reads remain retryable; nonworkspace folder forms are deliberately not retained.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: inspected resolveLocation's entire call path and both cache implementations; the changed initializer does not participate in lookup or refresh decisions.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Exact restoration duration is not measured; no change to the blocking operations is present.
Scenarios.Verdict: No regression or concrete performance-regression fix. The only changed runtime expression replaces a one-call localization wrapper with the equivalent direct call.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the performance-review pass over the full one-file inventory and both diff hunks, comparing base 36e8c0289a5f29eae15a933263220d9895302ff6 to head b9f63fda1c692c81a0ece4ff8f811dd1e3c70457. No high-confidence performance regressions found. Static read-only review; no findings or regression-fix signals warranted.
